name: ads.txt Guru Connect
author: ads.txt Guru

sections.description:
ads.txt Guru is a revolutionary tool to eliminate the burden of maintaining website ads.txt files! The ads.txt Guru system allows you to manage your ads.txt files online, automatically validate your ads.txt files, and collaborate between publisher and ad network to automate ads.txt updates.

By allowing ad networks to manage their ads.txt records on your website without your intervention, the time-consuming process of manually updating your ads.txt files when ad networks make changes can now be totally eliminated.

The ads.txt Guru Connect plugin enables you to connect your ads.txt Guru account to your WordPress installation to automate your ads.txt file upload whenever you or a collaborator makes changes to your ads.txt file via the ads.txt Guru management system, this eliminates the need to connect your FTP account.

It does the same for your app-ads.txt file, the mobile app equivalent of ads.txt, which is published as a separate file on the developer website listed on your app store pages. Each file has its own path and its own custom records in the plugin, so the two are never mixed up.

Features & Benefits:

  • Automate your ads.txt management: No more text editors! Manage your ads.txt records for multiple domains from a simple online interface, on any device.
  • Collaborate with ad networks: Eliminate urgent updates and lost revenue, simply allow your ad networks to contribute to your ads.txt file and their ads.txt changes are automatically synchronized with your ads.txt file.
  • Built-in validation: Inherent validation eliminates ads.txt errors ensuring you don’t lose revenue and waste time correcting mistakes. Quickly create consistent & properly validated ads.txt files with ease.
  • Automatic uploads: No more uploads! Connect your WordPress installation and upload your latest ads.txt file with a single click, and optionally allow automatic uploads whenever a collaborator makes a change.
  • Version control: Made a mistake, or simply need to go back to an old version? Quickly revert to any past version of your ads.txt file at the click of a button.
  • Protection against fraud: Ensure you only collaborate with your trusted ad networks to avoid fraudulent ads.txt records creeping in and losing you valuable revenue.
  • Quick start: Don’t worry about creating a new ads.txt file, simply import your existing ads.txt file and be up and running in seconds.
sections.installation:
1. Create a directory called adstxt-guru-connect in your /wp-content/plugins/ directory.

  2. Upload all *.txt and *.php files to the /wp-content/plugins/adstxt-guru-connect/ directory.

  3. Activate the ads.txt Guru Connect through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.

  4. Go to ‘ads.txt Guru’ section listed in your WordPress administration panel menu.
sections.faq:
Is ads.txt Guru a free service?

Yes, ads.txt Guru is completely free and our free plan allows you to manage your ads.txt files on up to 10 websites. Paid plans are available offering enhanced features such as ads.txt version control, and access to the ads.txt Guru API.

Where can I find documentation for ads.txt Guru?

For comprehensive documentation please refer to the Support section on the ads.txt Guru website.

Does this plugin support app-ads.txt?

Yes, from version 1.2.0. app-ads.txt is a separate file from ads.txt, so the plugin keeps a separate path and separate custom records for it, and only writes it when your ads.txt Guru account has an app-ads.txt file for this website. If you only manage an ads.txt file, nothing changes and no app-ads.txt file is created.

Do you offer technical support?

Yes, we offer free technical support, to get in touch please proceed to the Contact Us section on the ads.txt Guru website.

How do I report a security problem?

Email security@adstxt.guru. Our disclosure policy, what we ask of researchers, and how plugin security fixes are released are set out at adstxt.guru/support/documentation/security/. The same contact is published in machine-readable form at adstxt.guru/.well-known/security.txt.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

Detects a path left behind by a site move, instead of failing silently

  • The plugin now checks the configured path to your ads.txt and app-ads.txt files every time you open its page, and tells you when that path can no longer be written to. Previously the path was only checked when you saved the form, which meant the path the plugin sets for itself when it is first installed was never checked at all.
  • When a site moves to different hosting, the settings move with it but the directory layout does not, so the stored path ends up describing the old server and every update fails. The plugin now names this specifically and offers a ‘Use This Path’ button to set the path to this installation’s own root.
  • The connection test now fails when the file cannot be written, instead of reporting success. It previously only checked files that already existed, so a path whose directory had been removed passed the test and then failed every update.
  • An update that cannot write the file now reports that the location is unwritable, rather than reporting a generic failure.

1.2.0

app-ads.txt support, plus security and metadata corrections

  • app-ads.txt files are now updated by the plugin, with their own path and their own custom records, kept separately from your ads.txt file so neither can overwrite the other. Nothing is written to app-ads.txt unless ads.txt Guru asks for it.
  • ads.txt Guru names the file in both halves of the update request, and the plugin confirms which file it is writing before writing it. An installation running an older version of the plugin is not sent app-ads.txt content at all, so it cannot write it to the wrong file.
  • The file path form no longer requires the file to already exist, as long as its directory is writable. app-ads.txt usually will not exist yet.
  • Security: the path guard now rejects a directory whose name merely starts with the WordPress installation path, and rejects a home path that cannot be resolved rather than accepting any directory.
  • Security: the connection key, secret and token parameter are generated with wp_rand() rather than rand().
  • Saving custom records now reports a file it could not write instead of always reporting success.
  • Corrected plugin metadata: ‘Requires at least’ is 3.0 (site_url(), used since 1.0.0, was added in WordPress 3.0) and ‘Requires PHP’ is 5.4 (JSON_PRETTY_PRINT). Both were understated. Tested on WordPress 6.9.4, 7.0.4 and 7.1 (RC3).

1.1.2

Security hardening and improvements

1.1.1

Fixed plugin metadata: reduced tags to comply with 5 tag limit, added GPLv2 license declaration.

1.1.0

Custom ads.txt records feature added. Additional ads.txt records can be configured via the plugin which are then appended to the ads.txt file generated by the ads.txt Guru system.

1.0.2

Minor changes to improve plugin text.

1.0.1

Update to resolve connection issues.

1.0.0

First official release of plugin.
